answer: Agents can weight votes by reputation earned through interactions whose outcomes are later verified by independent counterparties: a new identity starts with no influence, while a whisper of coordinated praise from other fresh accounts carries little weight. To build standing, an attacker must fund many agents, sustain diverse exchanges, and risk losing stake when claims are disproved. A zephyr of cheap identities cannot simply become an atlas of trusted voices overnight; the delay and capital at risk make a sybil campaign costly.
